title: U.S. House · Texas's 34th District
area: A South Texas district covering the Rio Grande Valley, including Brownsville and McAllen.

context.text: Rep. Vicente Gonzalez Jr. is the incumbent under Texas's 2026 congressional map. Eric Flores won the Republican nomination.

summary.text: Vicente Gonzalez Jr. is the Democratic incumbent for Texas's 34th District. He is a South Texas attorney who opened his own law practice in 1997 and was first elected to Congress in 2016, representing the 15th District from 2017 to 2023 and the 34th since 2023. He sits on the House Financial Services Committee and says he is running on lowering costs, including drug prices and insulin costs, and ending tariffs.

background.text: According to Wikipedia, he was born on September 4, 1967, in Corpus Christi, Texas. His House biography describes him as a lifetime resident of South Texas, and his campaign website says he was raised in a military family.

Earned his GED in 1985, an associate degree in banking and finance from Del Mar College in 1990, a bachelor's degree in business aviation from Embry-Riddle University in 1992, and a J.D. from Texas Wesleyan University School of Law (now Texas A&M School of Law) in 1996.
His campaign website says he served as a congressional intern in Washington, D.C., during law school and later trained in negotiation at Harvard University School of Law.

Opened his law practice, V. Gonzalez & Associates, in 1997. His campaign website says his practice focused on suits against corporations on behalf of working families and on recovering money for South Texas school districts.

Was first elected to the U.S. House in 2016 to represent Texas's 15th District, after Rep. Rubén Hinojosa retired, and won re-election in 2018 and 2020. After redistricting, he has represented the 34th District since 2023, defeating Mayra Flores in both 2022 and 2024.

Has served on the House Committee on Financial Services in every Congress since 2017, including its Capital Markets subcommittee and its subcommittee on National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions. He also served on the Committee on Foreign Affairs from 2019 to 2022.

Chairs the Congressional Oil & Gas Caucus and co-chairs the Critical Minerals Caucus. He is also a member of the Blue Dog Coalition (where he is a Communications and Outreach Co-Chair), the New Democrat Coalition, the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, and the U.S.-Mexico Interparliamentary Group.
According to his House biography, he is married to Lorena Saenz Gonzalez, a former teacher and school administrator in Edinburg and McAllen, and they live in the Rio Grande Valley.

priorities.text: Chairs the Congressional Oil and Gas Caucus and supports an "all-the-above" energy approach.
priorities.quote: Congressman Gonzalez supports an all-the-above approach to energy and understands the importance of American energy not only to power our cars and homes, but also as a national security issue and a job creator.

priorities.text: Supports agricultural research, trade assistance, and crop insurance and disaster assistance programs for South Texas farmers and ranchers.
Says he works to lower health care costs and expand coverage, particularly for South Texas's uninsured and underinsured population.

positions.summary: Says he works to develop ideas that lower health care costs and provide better coverage, citing South Texas's large uninsured population.
Supports reducing barriers to the workforce, including lowering education costs and increasing access to childcare.
Supports an "all-the-above" energy approach that includes continued oil and gas production alongside other energy sources, rather than a faster transition away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: Congressman Gonzalez supports an all-the-above approach to energy

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Financial Services in the 2025-2026 (119th) Congress.
Chairs the Congressional Oil and Gas Caucus.

summary.text: Eric Flores is the Republican nominee for Texas's 34th District. He is an attorney and Army veteran who grew up in the Rio Grande Valley and worked as a city attorney, municipal judge, and assistant U.S. attorney before becoming a law firm partner. He won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary and says he is running to secure the border, lower costs, and improve infrastructure.

background.text: Grew up in the Rio Grande Valley, according to Fox News, which describes him as a Spanish speaker.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas at Austin and a J.D. from Texas Southern University.

Was commissioned in the U.S. Army as an infantry officer and rose to the rank of captain, according to Fox News. He later served in the Texas Army National Guard, where he commanded soldiers during Operation Guardian Support on the southern border.
Served as a city attorney and municipal judge, including as a municipal judge in Alton, Texas, before joining the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas.

Worked as an assistant U.S. attorney in the Southern District of Texas's McAllen Criminal Division, where KRGV reports he prosecuted members of cartel-connected and human-smuggling networks. His campaign biography, as quoted by Fox News, says he secured the conviction of a fugitive on Texas's "Top Ten" most-wanted list and received two U.S. Attorney's Awards.
Is a partner at O'Hanlon, Demerath & Castillo, a statewide law firm, where he leads the litigation department defending municipalities and school districts across Texas.
Launched his campaign for Congress in 2025 and advanced from the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Fox News reports he is married with two children.

priorities.text: Says he supports securing the border and law enforcement.
Says he will defend the Second Amendment and advocate for veterans and U.S. energy independence.
Says he will support President Trump's agenda.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for defending the Second Amendment.

summary.text: Eddie Espinoza is the Green Party nominee for Texas's 34th District. He is a U.S. Army veteran of Operation Desert Storm and a retired Rio Grande Valley public school teacher with 26 years in the classroom. He previously appeared on the 2024 ballot as the Green Party candidate for Texas Railroad Commissioner, and describes his campaign as centered on the environment and campaign finance reform.

background.text: Born in Dallas, Texas, and graduated from Mission High School.

Served in the U.S. Army from 1989 to 1991. In his Candidate Connection survey, he says he enlisted at 19, drove a Bradley fighting vehicle, and earned a combat infantry badge for service in Operation Desert Storm.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas-Pan American in 1994; he says he graduated through the GI Bill.
Taught in Rio Grande Valley public schools for 26 years before retiring, teaching reading and math, according to his Candidate Connection survey.
Was the Green Party candidate for Texas Railroad Commissioner in 2024 and advanced from the Green Party's March 21, 2026 convention as its nominee for U.S. House.

priorities.text: Supports plugging and decommissioning idle oil and gas wells he says are contaminating water sources.
Supports banning fracking and stopping new fossil-fuel infrastructure, including proposed LNG export terminals on the Gulf Coast.

positions.summary: Supports banning fracking, halting new fossil-fuel infrastructure, and decarbonizing the Texas economy.
positions.quote: Let's ban fracking and stop the expansion of new fossil fuels infrastructure and projects, including proposed LNG export terminals along the Gulf coast. Decarbonize the Texas economy, and make it more resilient to global warming.

summary.text: Chris Royal is the Libertarian Party nominee for Texas's 34th District. He is an Army veteran, attorney, and retired teacher who moved to the Rio Grande Valley in 1993 and has run for this seat before as an independent. In his 2024 Candidate Connection survey, he said he is running to reduce federal spending and have existing immigration laws enforced.

background.text: Born in Kokomo, Indiana; says his family moved to Springfield, Missouri, when he was 12, where his father ran a restaurant and he worked.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Southwest Missouri State University in 1982 (he says in philosophy, with a minor in ancient history).

Served in the U.S. Army from 1982 to 1990, including at the Pentagon and with the 1st Infantry Division at Fort Riley, Kansas, and says he was called up for Operation Desert Storm and served at Fort McPherson, Georgia.
Earned a J.D. from the Kansas City School of Law in 1990, according to his survey.

Says he spent a year in Arkansas teaching himself C++ and writing a real estate textbook. Ballotpedia lists his career experience as teacher, lawyer, real estate textbook author, computer programmer, and restaurateur.
Moved permanently to the Rio Grande Valley in 1993, holding jobs in the legal, title, and teaching fields, and retired from teaching in 2024, according to his survey.

Ran for this seat as an independent in 2022, receiving 4,079 votes (3.0%). Ballotpedia lists him as a withdrawn or disqualified independent candidate in 2024, and he is the Libertarian nominee in 2026 after the party's March 21, 2026 convention.
According to his survey, he is married with two children and attends Holy Family Catholic Church in Brownsville.

priorities.text: Says immigration laws already on the books should be enforced.
priorities.quote: If elected, I vote to execute the laws on the books with respect to illegal border crossings.

positions.summary: Says he supports enforcing existing immigration laws regarding illegal border crossings.
positions.quote: If elected, I vote to execute the laws on the books with respect to illegal border crossings.
